stimulus.title: Earthquake Distance and Shaking
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Seismologists compared the maximum ground motion recorded by identical seismographs at several distances from the epicenter of an earthquake. All stations stood on the same type of bedrock.
Results (the maximum ground motion): at 50 km, 4.87 mm; at 100 km, 1.72 mm; at 150 km, 0.94 mm; at 200 km, 0.61 mm.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following is a controlled variable, kept the same in every trial?

choices.rationale: The distance from the speaker was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The sound intensity was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The brand of the speaker is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

choices.text: The height of the sound meter
choices.rationale: Correct. The height of the sound meter was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

explanation: Only the distance from the speaker was varied and only the sound intensity was measured; the height of the sound meter was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: In an open field, students placed a speaker playing a steady tone and used a sound meter to measure the intensity at several distances along a straight line from the speaker. Readings were taken at the same height above the ground. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Why did the experimenters most likely include a trial at a catalyst mass of 0 mg?

choices.text: Check that the instrument used to measure the time for the reaction to finish was properly calibrated
choices.rationale: Nothing in the procedure uses the zero trial to calibrate an instrument.

choices.text: Produce the largest possible value of the time for the reaction to finish in the experiment
choices.rationale: The 0 mg row is a baseline, not an attempt to obtain a maximum.

choices.text: Serve as a control against which the other trials could be compared
choices.rationale: Correct. A zero trial shows what happens with none of the treatment, so the effect of each nonzero amount can be judged against it.

choices.text: Determine whether the volume of hydrogen peroxide has any effect on the time for the reaction to finish
choices.rationale: The volume of hydrogen peroxide was held constant, so no trial can test its effect.

explanation: A trial with catalyst mass of zero serves as the control: it establishes the baseline value of the time for the reaction to finish against which the other trials are compared.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students mixed 50 mL of hydrogen peroxide solution from a single bottle with a measured mass of powdered catalyst and timed how long it took for the bubbling to stop. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following trials was the control trial?

choices.text: The trial at 4 mg, in the middle of the tested range of catalyst mass
choices.rationale: A middle value still applies the treatment; it is not a baseline.

choices.text: The trial at the greatest catalyst mass, 6 mg, which received the most treatment
choices.rationale: The largest dose is a test condition, not the baseline.

choices.text: The trial at 0 mg, which received none of the treatment being tested
choices.rationale: Correct. The trial with none of the treatment shows the baseline that every other trial is compared against.

choices.text: The trial that produced the greatest reaction time
choices.rationale: A control is defined by its treatment (none), not by the size of its result.

stimulus.title: Enzyme Activity and pH
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students added 1 mL of enzyme solution to tubes containing a substrate solution buffered to a set pH. They measured how much product formed in 5 minutes to find the activity. Each pH was tested in triplicate.
Results (the activity of the enzyme): at pH 3, 8 µmol/min; at pH 4, 24 µmol/min; at pH 5, 46 µmol/min; at pH 6, 51 µmol/min; at pH 7, 34 µmol/min.
